options.text: A device that generates electricity from solar panels
The network of cables, pylons, and transformers that distributes electricity across the country
A type of battery that stores electricity
A single power station that supplies the whole country

questions.explanation: The National Grid is the network of cables, pylons, and transformers that distributes electricity from power stations to homes and businesses across the country.

questions.stem: Why is electricity transmitted at very high voltages (up to 400 kV)?

options.text: Because generators can only produce high-voltage electricity
Because high voltage makes the electricity travel faster
Because high voltage is safer for the public
Because high voltage means low current, which reduces energy lost as heat in the cables

questions.explanation: For the same power (P = IV), increasing the voltage reduces the current. Since power lost in cables equals I squared R, reducing the current dramatically reduces the energy wasted as heat in the transmission cables.

questions.stem: What type of transformer is used at the power station end of the National Grid?

options.text: A step-up transformer
An isolation transformer
A step-down transformer
No transformer is needed

questions.explanation: A step-up transformer at the power station increases the voltage from about 25 kV to 275 kV or 400 kV for efficient long-distance transmission, reducing the current and therefore the energy lost in cables.

questions.stem: If the current in a transmission cable is halved, by what factor does the power loss in the cable change?

options.text: It is reduced to one quarter
It is halved
It is doubled
It stays the same

questions.explanation: Power loss in cables is given by P = I squared R. If the current is halved, the power loss becomes (I/2) squared x R = I squared R / 4, which is one quarter of the original loss.

questions.stem: Why does the National Grid use AC rather than DC?

options.text: Because transformers only work with AC, and transformers are essential for stepping voltage up and down
Because AC is safer than DC
Because AC can be stored more easily than DC
Because DC cannot flow through cables

questions.explanation: Transformers require a changing current to create a changing magnetic field, so they only work with AC. The National Grid relies on transformers to step voltage up for efficient transmission and step it down for safe domestic use.

questions.stem: What voltage is electricity supplied to homes in the UK?

options.text: 25 kV
132 kV
400 kV

questions.explanation: Electricity is supplied to UK homes at 230 V AC, 50 Hz. Multiple step-down transformers at substations progressively reduce the transmission voltage from 400 kV down to 230 V for safe domestic use.

questions.stem: What is one advantage of underground cables over overhead power lines?

options.text: They have no visual impact on the landscape
They are naturally cooled by the air
They are easier to repair
They are cheaper to install

questions.explanation: Underground cables have no visual impact on the landscape, unlike pylons which can be considered unsightly. However, underground cables are much more expensive to install (10-20 times the cost) and harder to repair.
